hypotheses: Selumetinib is a MEK1/2 inhibitor; in A375 (BRAF V600E) cells, MEK inhibition can alter MAPK-driven chromatin-modifier expression/activity, producing reproducible histone-mark changes such as H3K27me3K36me0 loss and H3K9ac/K14ac gain.

Donors with high anchor similarity and/or MAPK-pathway or chromatin-linked pharmacology (TG101348, Dinaciclib, vemurafenib, flavopiridol, Verteporfin) are most likely to transfer a target-minus-A375 histone response that matches the query signature.

The query's strongest anchor features are H3K27me3K36me0 and H3K27me2K36me1 decreases with H3K9me1K14ac0 and H3K9ac1K14ac0 increases, suggesting a shift from repressive H3K27 methylation toward H3K9 acetylation; donor selection should prioritize compounds whose measured responses can reproduce this direction.
object.evidence_gap: No donor response values are provided; only anchor similarity and structure similarity are available. The PubChem description confirms MEK1/2 inhibition but does not establish that any candidate donor shares the same histone-mark response. Measured donor target-minus-A375 profiles are needed to verify a reproducible >0.5 log2 histone perturbation and to avoid selecting donors based on pharmacology alone.
